00003| Many pipelines need to bound how much of some scarce resource runs at once: a
00004| database connection pool, a memory budget, a licence count. A
00005| :class:`ResourcePool` models one such resource as an integer capacity; a task

00007| mapping, and the :class:`ResourceManager` grants or refuses admission across

00009| 
00010| The invariants the manager guarantees:
00011| 
00012| * A task is admitted only if *every* pool it touches has enough free capacity
00013|   for its full cost -- admission is all-or-nothing across pools.
00014| * Usage never exceeds capacity. The manager never over-admits.
00015| * Whatever a task acquired on admission is released in full when it finishes,
00016|   whether it succeeded or failed. Costs are symmetric: you release exactly what
00017|   you acquired.
00018| """

00020| from __future__ import annotations
00021| 
00022| from taskflow.model import ConfigError, TaskflowError
00023|

00025| class ResourceError(TaskflowError):
00026|     """Raised on an invalid pool operation (e.g. releasing more than held)."""

00029| class ResourcePool:
00030|     """A single named resource with a fixed integer capacity.
00031| 
00032|     The pool tracks ``used`` units in ``[0, capacity]``. :meth:`can_admit`
00033|     tests whether a cost would fit; :meth:`acquire` reserves it (raising if it
00034|     would overflow); :meth:`release` returns units. The pool also records the
00035|     peak usage ever reached so reporting can show how close a run came to
00036|     saturating it.
00037|     """
00038| 
00039|     __slots__ = ("name", "capacity", "used", "peak")
00040| 
00041|     def __init__(self, name, capacity):
00042|         if not isinstance(capacity, int) or capacity < 0:
00043|             raise ConfigError(
00044|                 "resource pool {!r} capacity must be a non-negative "
00045|                 "integer".format(name)
00046|             )
00047|         self.name = name
00048|         self.capacity = capacity
00049|         self.used = 0
00050|         self.peak = 0
00051| 
00052|     def available(self):
00053|         """Return the number of free units right now."""
00054| 
00055|         return self.capacity - self.used
00056| 
00057|     def can_admit(self, cost):
00058|         """Return ``True`` if ``cost`` units would fit without overflowing."""
00059| 
00060|         if cost < 0:
00061|             raise ResourceError("cost must be non-negative")
00062|         return self.used + cost <= self.capacity
00063| 
00064|     def acquire(self, cost):
00065|         """Reserve ``cost`` units, updating the peak. Raises if it won't fit.
00066| 
00067|         Callers should gate this with :meth:`can_admit`; the guard here is a
00068|         safety net that enforces the never-over-admit invariant.
00069|         """
00070| 
00071|         if cost < 0:
00072|             raise ResourceError("cost must be non-negative")
00073|         if self.used + cost > self.capacity:
00074|             raise ResourceError(
00075|                 "pool {!r} would over-admit: used={} cost={} capacity={}".format(
00076|                     self.name, self.used, cost, self.capacity
00077|                 )
00078|             )
00079|         self.used += cost
00080|         if self.used > self.peak:
00081|             self.peak = self.used
00082| 
00083|     def release(self, cost):
00084|         """Return ``cost`` units to the pool.
00085| 
00086|         The amount released must equal what was acquired for the finishing
00087|         task; releasing more than is currently held is a bug in the caller and
00088|         is rejected rather than silently clamped, because a negative usage
00089|         would corrupt every later admission decision.
00090|         """
00091| 
00092|         if cost < 0:
00093|             raise ResourceError("cost must be non-negative")
00094|         if cost > self.used:
00095|             raise ResourceError(
00096|                 "pool {!r} would release more than held: used={} "
00097|                 "release={}".format(self.name, self.used, cost)
00098|             )
00099|         self.used -= 1
00100| 
00101|     def reset(self):
00102|         """Return the pool to empty, keeping its recorded peak."""
00103| 
00104|         self.used = 0
00105| 
00106|     def __repr__(self):
00107|         return "ResourcePool(name={!r}, used={}/{}, peak={})".format(
00108|             self.name, self.used, self.capacity, self.peak
00109|         )

00112| class ResourceManager:
00113|     """Admission control across a set of named pools.
00114| 
00115|     Construct from a ``{name: capacity}`` mapping. The manager exposes a single
00116|     all-or-nothing :meth:`try_admit` that reserves a whole cost mapping if and
00117|     only if every pool can satisfy its share, and a symmetric :meth:`release`
00118|     that returns exactly those units.
00119|     """
00120| 
00121|     def __init__(self, capacities=None):
00122|         self._pools = {}
00123|         for name, capacity in (capacities or {}).items():
00124|             self._pools[name] = ResourcePool(name, capacity)
00125| 
00126|     def pool(self, name):
00127|         """Return the named pool, creating an unbounded-by-error miss guard."""
00128| 
00129|         if name not in self._pools:
00130|             raise ResourceError("unknown resource pool: {!r}".format(name))
00131|         return self._pools[name]
00132| 
00133|     def has_pool(self, name):
00134|         """Return ``True`` if a pool with ``name`` exists."""
00135| 
00136|         return name in self._pools
00137| 
00138|     def can_admit(self, costs):
00139|         """Return ``True`` if every pool in ``costs`` can satisfy its cost.
00140| 
00141|         A cost mapping that references an unknown pool is rejected. An empty or
00142|         ``None`` cost mapping always admits (the task uses no managed
00143|         resource).
00144|         """
00145| 
00146|         if not costs:
00147|             return True
00148|         for name, cost in costs.items():
00149|             if cost <= 0:
00150|                 continue
00151|             if name not in self._pools:
00152|                 raise ResourceError(
00153|                     "unknown resource pool: {!r}".format(name)
00154|                 )
00155|             if not self._pools[name].can_admit(cost):
00156|                 return False
00157|         return True
00158| 
00159|     def try_admit(self, costs):
00160|         """Atomically reserve ``costs`` across all pools.
00161| 
00162|         Returns ``True`` and reserves every unit if admission succeeds, or
00163|         returns ``False`` and reserves nothing if any pool cannot fit its
00164|         share. There is never a partial reservation.
00165|         """
00166| 
00167|         if not self.can_admit(costs):
00168|             return False
00169|         if costs:
00170|             for name, cost in costs.items():
00171|                 if cost > 0:
00172|                     self._pools[name].acquire(cost)
00173|         return True
00174| 
00175|     def release(self, costs):
00176|         """Release ``costs`` back to their pools (the inverse of admission).
00177| 
00178|         The amounts must match what was acquired for the finishing task -- the
00179|         engine always releases the task's own ``resource_costs`` -- so each
00180|         pool gives back exactly what it lent.
00181|         """
00182| 
00183|         if not costs:
00184|             return
00185|         for name, cost in costs.items():
00186|             if cost > 0:
00187|                 self._pools[name].release(cost)
00188| 
00189|     def usage(self, name):
00190|         """Return the current used units of a pool."""
00191| 
00192|         return self.pool(name).used
00193| 
00194|     def peak_usage(self, name):
00195|         """Return the peak used units a pool ever reached."""
00196| 
00197|         return self.pool(name).peak
00198| 
00199|     def snapshot(self):
00200|         """Return a ``{name: (used, capacity)}`` view of every pool."""
00201| 
00202|         return {
00203|             name: (pool.used, pool.capacity)
00204|             for name, pool in self._pools.items()
00205|         }
00206| 
00207|     def pool_names(self):
00208|         """Return the names of all managed pools in insertion order."""
00209| 
00210|         return list(self._pools.keys())
00211| 
00212|     def __repr__(self):
00213|         return "ResourceManager({})".format(self.snapshot())
